close_reason: fixed: removed excluded loop from nc_constrained_types seeding
description: Trigger: anchor NC has excluded_subtrees=[dNSName:.evil.com] with no permitted_subtrees; later intermediate CA has permitted_subtrees=[iPAddress:10.0.0.0/8]. The anchor seeding loop (chain_walk lines ~1230-1233) ORs NC_TYPE_DNS into nc_constrained_types from the excluded entry. When the intermediate's permitted_subtrees transitions nc_permitted from None to Some([iPAddress:...]), the permitted check fires for all constrained types. dNSName type has its bit set (from the anchor excluded loop) but no entry in nc_permitted — every leaf with a dNSName SAN receives NameConstraintViolation. Bad behavior: false rejection of valid chains. The excluded check (require_match=false) does NOT use nc_constrained_types at all, so setting excluded-type bits there serves no legitimate purpose and only causes this false-positive. The existing PKIX-onc.18 note claims this seeding is 'critically correct' but that reasoning is wrong: the excluded check fires unconditionally without consulting nc_constrained_types.
title: nc_constrained_types seeded from anchor excluded: false NC violation
